scope_note: Authoritative Mercury encounter source recovery for DS port. Runtime tables are already-authored Mercury GBA encounter tables. Staged registries preserve authored Platinum/Sinnoh ecology that had not yet been wired into the old runtime.

missing.scope: Whole-Sinnoh missing-area encounter audit — Route 205 North, Ravaged Path, Old Chateau, Snowpoint Temple, Routes 219-221 / Pal Park approach
missing.design_source: Pokemon Platinum / Sinnoh, expanded for Mercury Redux
missing.source_rule: Platinum/Sinnoh is the content source. Internal engine identifiers are implementation-only and do not define geography, ecology, or encounter design.

ROUTE_205_NORTH.identity: Platinum north half: Bidoof/Budew/Wurmple/Silcoon/Cascoon/Kricketot with rare Beautifly/Dustox; Mercury adds a forest-edge riverside layer without replacing those anchors.
ROUTE_205_NORTH.special_normalization: Platinum Poké Radar Slowpoke is folded into the normal authored pool. GBA cartridge-insertion Lotad is not used as a source mechanic.

RAVAGED_PATH.identity: Small Platinum Route 204 cave. Current Mercury land roster remains anchored by Zubat/Psyduck and expanded cave species; missing Surf/fishing ecology is restored from Platinum structure.

OLD_CHATEAU.identity: Platinum haunted mansion where ordinary wild encounters are Gastly-only; Mercury retains Gastly as the dominant anchor and expands with fitting Ghost species while preserving the manor as a special haunted location.

rotom.respawn: Next night / on re-entry after date rollover if KO or fled

OLD_CHATEAU.secret_key_policy: Rotom form appliances/Secret Key become an in-game unlock after the Old Chateau encounter; no external distribution requirement.

SNOWPOINT_TEMPLE.identity: Platinum temple retains Golbat/Sneasel plus Smoochum on 1F and Jynx on deeper floors; Mercury diversifies the frozen temple gradually without replacing those anchors.

regigigas.requirement: Regirock, Regice, and Registeel in party
regigigas.pre_league_policy: Temple entry and Regigigas encounter must not require National Dex or Hall of Fame once the three Regis are obtainable.

ROUTE_219.identity: Platinum small beach route south of Sandgem: no land grass, Surf/fishing only, anchored by Tentacool/Wingull/Tentacruel/Pelipper.

ROUTE_220.identity: Platinum open sea route with small islands. Keeps the Route 219 coastal anchors but shifts toward deeper-water species and stronger fishing targets.

ROUTE_221.identity: Platinum wooded Pal Park approach anchored by Sudowoodo/Girafarig/Roselia/Floatzel. Radar Nidorina/Nidorino and swarm Farfetchd are normalized into authored encounters instead of special RNG.

PAL_PARK.identity: Preserve Platinum Pal Park as a special facility rather than inventing a normal grass table. Mercury can later repurpose its migration function, but ordinary route-style encounters are intentionally absent.

remaining_audit_flags: Regirock/Regice/Registeel pre-League access still needs a dedicated Platinum-ruins policy. Registeel Iron Ruins is already reserved on Iron Island; Iceberg Ruins is in Mt. Coronet; Rock Peak Ruins is normally on postgame Route 228 and needs a Mercury pre-League access solution without using external-event Regigigas.
Battle Zone / Routes 225-230 have not been part of the main pre-League encounter pass. No required species may depend on those postgame routes.

northern.scope: Fuego Ironworks + northern Sinnoh snow progression
northern.design_source: Pokemon Platinum / Sinnoh, expanded for Mercury Redux
northern.source_rule: Platinum/Sinnoh defines geography, encounter anchors, ecology, and progression. Emerald-derived engine IDs are hidden implementation infrastructure only and are not content sources.
northern.runtime_note: The cumulative source does not yet contain finished player-facing Sinnoh maps for Fuego Ironworks, Route 216, Route 217, Acuity Lakefront, Lake Acuity, or Snowpoint City. These tables are authoritative staged encounter specifications and must only be wired when the actual Platinum-derived maps exist.

FUEGO_IRONWORKS.identity: Optional industrial riverside habitat. Platinum anchors Magnemite, Magmar, Floatzel, and Gastrodon; Mercury adds Fire/Electric/forge species without turning the area into a generic cave.
notes: Platinum makes Magmar and Magnemite signature Fuego encounters.
Honey remains instant in Mercury: one Honey triggers one immediate premium encounter; no waiting/cooldown.

ROUTE_216.identity: Snowy treeline and mountain-pass ecology. Platinum Snover/Sneasel/Meditite/Graveler backbone; Mercury introduces cold forest and mountain species.
notes: Night increases Snorunt and nocturnal/ghostly cold-weather species.
No invented water table; Platinum Route 216 is treated as a land snow route.

ROUTE_217.identity: Deep-blizzard tundra. Platinum Snover/Swinub/Sneasel/Snorunt identity; Mercury expands with harsher Ice species distinct from Route 216.

icy_rock.purpose: Glaceon evolution landmark; do not replace with a generic item trigger.

ACUITY_LAKEFRONT.identity: High-elevation snow shelf at the Lake Acuity approach. Platinum Snover/Swinub/Sneasel backbone; Mercury emphasizes evolved cold-climate species.
notes: Glaceon is a very rare wild reward here, while the Route 217 Icy Rock remains the normal evolution landmark.

LAKE_ACUITY.identity: Northern lake-edge snow-and-water habitat. Platinum Snover/Bibarel/Golduck/Sneasel/Psyduck backbone retained.

cave.note: Uxie remains a static/story encounter rather than a generic cave wild table.

SNOWPOINT_CITY.note: No wild table is invented for the city itself. Snowpoint's encounter identity belongs to its surrounding routes/lake unless a later Platinum map source explicitly supports otherwise.

diversification_rules: Adjacent northern areas share only ecologically necessary Platinum anchors; Mercury additions are intentionally different by biome.
Great Marsh Safari-exclusive foreign rares remain reserved and are not reused as ordinary northern-route catches.
Fuego Ironworks remains an optional side-area with a Fire/Electric/industrial identity rather than a substitute for normal route Fire availability.
No player-facing geography is derived from Emerald/Hoenn; runtime wiring waits for actual Sinnoh maps.

route210_north.design_source: Pokemon Platinum Route 210 North, expanded for Mercury Redux
route210_north.source_rule: Platinum/Sinnoh defines ecology and geography. Engine map IDs are not design sources.
route210_north.runtime_note: The cumulative source does not yet contain a finished player-facing Route 210 North map. This registry is intentionally not bound to an unrelated engine map. Wire it when the Platinum/Sinnoh Route 210 North map is constructed.

celestic_town.correction_note: Platinum Celestic Town has water encounters; previous no-wild statement applied only to land/ruins and is superseded.

route211.area: Route 211 West + Route 211 East + Mt. Coronet Route 211 entrance + Celestic water correction
route211.design_source: Pokemon Platinum Route 211 / Mt. Coronet / Celestic Town, expanded for Mercury Redux
route211.source_rule: Platinum/Sinnoh defines geography and ecology. Emerald-derived identifiers are hidden engine infrastructure only and are not design sources.
route211.runtime_note: The cumulative source does not yet contain finished player-facing Route 211 West/East or the full Route 211-side Mt. Coronet map chain. These encounters are intentionally staged and must be wired only when the corresponding Sinnoh maps exist.

route211_west.availability: Optional Eterna-side segment; reachable much earlier than the Celestic-side segment.
route211_west.note: No invented Surf/fishing table; wild water is not added unless the final Platinum-derived map/source supports it.

route211_east.availability: Celestic-side segment after the northern Route 210/Celestic progression.
route211_east.note: Retains Platinum Route 211 East Honey Tree concept using Mercury instant-Honey rules.

mt_coronet_route211_lower_cavern.note: Deeper Route 211-side Coronet progression; authored separately so Mt. Coronet is not one generic cave roster.

celestic_town_correction.note: Correction to prior Route 210 North registry: Platinum Celestic Town has water encounters. Celestic Ruins remain random-encounter free.

diversity_rules: Route 211 West and East are separate ecological/level identities because Mt. Coronet divides the route.
Route 211 East must not simply copy Route 210 North despite geographic continuity.
Mt. Coronet entrance and lower cavern have separate encounter rosters.
Great Marsh Safari-exclusive species remain reserved and are not reused here.

route218.design_source: Pokemon Platinum Route 218 and Canalave City, expanded for Mercury Redux
route218.source_rule: Platinum/Sinnoh defines geography, ecology, and encounter identity. Emerald-derived map constants are hidden engine infrastructure only and are not design sources.
route218.runtime_note: The cumulative source does not yet contain finished player-facing Route 218 and Canalave City Sinnoh maps. These encounters are intentionally staged and must be wired only when those Platinum-derived maps exist.

route218.identity: Short Surf-heavy fishing route west of Jubilife, transitioning into Canalave maritime/industrial ecology.
notes: Mr. Mime remains a prominent Route 218 catch, preserving Platinum identity.
Chatot is absent at Night, preserving Platinum time-of-day behavior.
Voltorb is integrated as a low-rate regular encounter rather than a swarm-only daily gate.
The Mercury expansion leans into Canalave-bound industrial/coastal species rather than repeating Route 213 beach/tide-pool ecology.

canalave_city.note: Canalave water intentionally overlaps Route 218 because it is the same connected waterway. Mercury adds a modest harbor-specific Super Rod layer without erasing the Platinum core.

diversity_rules: Do not reuse Great Marsh Safari-exclusive species as ordinary Route 218 or Canalave catches.
Route 218 must remain distinct from Route 213: industrial/coastal approach rather than beach/tide-pool ecology.
Shared Route 218/Canalave aquatic species are intentional because the areas share one connected waterway.
Do not bind staged data to unrelated non-Sinnoh maps.

route222.scope: Spear Pillar / Distortion World encounter policy + Route 222 / Sunyshore encounter specification
route222.design_source: Pokemon Platinum / Sinnoh, expanded for Mercury Redux
route222.source_rule: Platinum/Sinnoh defines geography, encounter anchors, ecology, and progression. Emerald-derived engine IDs are hidden implementation infrastructure only and are not content sources.
route222.runtime_note: The final player-facing Spear Pillar, Distortion World, Route 222, and Sunyshore maps are not yet constructed in this cumulative source. Do not attach these encounter specs to unrelated engine geography.

story_encounters: Dialga/Palkia remain story-controlled during the Galactic climax; they are not random encounters.
Giratina interrupts Cyrus and opens the Distortion World as in Platinum.

DISTORTION_WORLD.reason: Platinum explicitly has no ordinary wild Pokémon in the Distortion World. Its emptiness is preserved as part of the area identity.

scripted_static.role: Mandatory story/static encounter at the end of the Distortion World

DISTORTION_WORLD.retry_policy: Mercury QoL: if Giratina is defeated or the player flees, the story encounter remains recoverable before the League rather than becoming a postgame-only loss. Exact reset/respawn script is staged for the final Distortion World map implementation.
DISTORTION_WORLD.time_policy: The global clock continues to exist for save/evolution systems, but Distortion World has no day/night encounter tables because it has no random encounters.
DISTORTION_WORLD.lake_guardians: Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf are story guides/puzzle actors here, not random encounters.
DISTORTION_WORLD.cyrus: Final Cyrus battle remains a scripted boss encounter before Giratina.

TURNBACK_CAVE_FUTURE_POLICY.note: Do not use Turnback Cave to justify random Distortion World encounters. It will receive its own Platinum-based cave audit later, including pre-League availability decisions needed by Mercury’s all-supported-Pokémon-before-postgame policy.

ROUTE_222.identity: Southeastern Sinnoh coastal route into Sunyshore. Platinum electric/coastal anchors remain, while Mercury adds evolved late-game electric and shoreline species instead of recycling Route 218/213 wholesale.
notes: Platinum anchors: Electabuzz, Floatzel, Magnemite, Wingull, Luxio, Chatot, Magneton, Pelipper.
Chatot is absent at Night, following Platinum time-of-day behavior.
Flaaffy/Skitty special encounter ideas from Platinum are not required as randomizer gates; Mercury uses authored TOD/rare distribution instead.
Honey is instant in Mercury: one Honey triggers one immediate premium encounter with no wait or cooldown.

SUNYSHORE_CITY.identity: Sunyshore itself has no random land encounters. Its harbor/sea water is a late-game coastal fishery connected to Route 222.
notes: Platinum Sunyshore water uses Tentacool/Wingull/Tentacruel/Pelipper as its core; Mercury expands the connected harbor ecology without inventing city grass encounters.

design_rules: Distortion World has no random wild encounters; Giratina Origin is a scripted static encounter.
Route 222 preserves Platinum electric/coastal anchors and Chatot day/night behavior.
Route 222 must feel distinct from Route 213 and Route 218 by emphasizing late-game evolved Electric species.
Sunyshore has no random land table; water/fishing only.
No Great Marsh Safari-exclusive species are reused as ordinary Route 222/Sunyshore catches.
Honey Tree remains instant and premium.

route223.scope: Route 223 / Pokemon League approach / Victory Road encounter specification
route223.design_source: Pokemon Platinum / Sinnoh, expanded for Mercury Redux
route223.source_rule: Platinum/Sinnoh defines geography, encounter anchors, ecology, and progression. Emerald-derived engine IDs are hidden implementation infrastructure only and are not content sources.
route223.runtime_note: Final player-facing Route 223, Pokemon League approach, and Victory Road maps are not yet constructed in this cumulative source. Do not attach these specs to unrelated engine geometry.

route_223.identity: Platinum Route 223 sea route: a fully aquatic final approach from Sunyshore to the Pokemon League, expanded with rare open-water species while retaining Tentacruel/Pelipper/Mantyke as the core.
notes: No land encounter table; Route 223 is a water route in Platinum.
Mercury raises the practical encounter levels to match its late-game progression.
Waterfall traversal remains governed by Mercury HM-free badge/story + compatible-party-Pokemon rules; no move-slot requirement.

victory_road.design: Main pre-League Victory Road remains Platinum-based 1F / 2F / B1F. Each floor preserves Platinum anchors but has a different Mercury identity. No generic Rock Smash encounters are invented because Platinum does not list a Rock Smash wild table here.

1F_ROCKY_GATE.identity: Rock/ground entry chamber. Platinum anchors Graveler, Onix, Rhyhorn/Rhydon, Golbat, Steelix and Gabite remain visible; Mercury adds late-game mineral/dragon targets.

2F_MAGNETIC_GALLERY.identity: Steel/magnetic upper chamber. Platinum Steelix/Magneton/Gabite core expanded with evolved Steel and Ground species.

B1F_UNDERGROUND_WATER.identity: Underground lake chamber. Platinum Azumarill/Floatzel plus cave anchors preserved, with a distinct Water/Fighting/Dragon expansion.

marley_branch_policy.platinum_reference: Platinum locks the Marley/Route 224 branch behind the National Dex. Mercury must not use that postgame lock because supported Pokemon are intended to be obtainable before the League/postgame.
marley_branch_policy.mercury_policy: Unlock the Marley branch through authored pre-League story/progression when its real Sinnoh map and Route 224 content are built. Keep its encounter tables separate from the main 1F/2F/B1F route.

league_approach.youngster_martin: Final mandatory Youngster Martin battle remains a scripted trainer encounter before the League; this ecology pass does not change his canonical team.

route224.scope: Pre-League Marley Victory Road branch / Route 224 / Seabreak Path / Flower Paradise encounter specification
route224.design_source: Pokemon Platinum / Sinnoh, expanded for Mercury Redux
route224.source_rule: Platinum/Sinnoh defines geography, ecology, encounters, and story placement. Emerald-derived engine IDs are hidden implementation infrastructure only and are never used as content sources.
route224.runtime_note: The finished Platinum-derived Marley branch, Route 224, Seabreak Path and Flower Paradise maps are not yet constructed in this cumulative source. Do not wire these specs onto unrelated engine geometry.

unlock_policy.platinum: The Marley branch opens only after the National Dex / postgame progression in Platinum.
unlock_policy.mercury: Open the branch during the first pre-League Victory Road visit after the player has the required story/badge traversal permissions. No National Dex or Hall of Fame gate.
unlock_policy.partner: Marley joins in the fog/underground branch as a battle partner using her Arcanine. Partner double-battle/healing behavior is preserved; this ecology pass does not rebalance her trainer data.

FOG_GALLERY.identity: Platinum Nat Dex Area converted into the pre-League Marley entrance: damp/foggy cave retaining Floatzel, Graveler, Onix, Golbat, Steelix and Gabite, with a stronger nocturnal/mineral expansion.

UNDERGROUND_LAKE.identity: Platinum Nat Dex Area B1F converted into the pre-League Marley lake: Azumarill, Floatzel, Dewgong, Graveler, Golbat and Gabite remain anchors; cold-water and cave species expand the hunt.

EXIT_PASSAGE.identity: Final Platinum Nat Dex Exit Area before Route 224; a stronger mixed rock/dragon passage that signals the route beyond.

route_224.identity: Platinum Route 224: remote forested peninsula with beaches and the White Rock, expanded as a pre-League optional high-level route.

platinum_specials_normalized.policy: Mercury folds these Platinum special-method species into authored TOD tables instead of requiring Radar/swarm RNG. GBA-cartridge insertion is not used as a content source.

route_224.white_rock: Preserved as the route endpoint and Shaymin/Seabreak Path story anchor.

white_rock_oaks_letter.platinum: Oak's Letter opens Seabreak Path from the White Rock after the gratitude interaction.
white_rock_oaks_letter.mercury: Oak's Letter becomes an obtainable in-game pre-League sidequest key item; no external distribution/event requirement. Exact quest giver/staging is deferred to the Route 224 story-map pass.

seabreak_path.role: Flower-covered approach to Flower Paradise; preserve Platinum's encounter-free presentation.

flower_paradise.gracidea_policy: Catching the fateful/static Shaymin should unlock the normal Gracidea/Sky Forme path in Mercury; exact NPC/item script is deferred.

great_marsh.engine_note: Current Safari-zone map constants are temporary internal implementation slots only and are not player-facing design sources.

daily_rng_policy.binoculars_role: informational discovery / area preview only; never gates species availability

safari_exclusive_policy.purpose: Each Great Marsh biome has a distinct pool of foreign Safari rares unavailable on ordinary authored Sinnoh routes.

great_marsh_exclusives.engine_note: Engine map constants are hidden implementation infrastructure only; they are not encounter/geography design sources.

safari_exclusive_policy.purpose: Each Great Marsh biome has a distinct pool of foreign Safari rares unavailable on ordinary authored Sinnoh routes.
